theme: Navigating Risk, Technology, and Growth in a Rapidly Changing Economy

agenda.title: Registration & Networking Breakfast
agenda.description: Time to connect with peers, speakers, and sponsors before formal sessions begin. Early networking helps CFOs and CEOs share immediate challenges and set context for the day’s discussions.

agenda.title: Welcome & Opening Remarks
agenda.speaker: Rod Nunez – Conference Chair / Host
agenda.description: Set expectations for the day, outline learning objectives, and emphasize how the agenda aligns with today’s CFO and CEO responsibilities—strategic leadership, risk management, technology adoption, and value creation.

agenda.title: Economic Outlook
agenda.speaker: John Norris – Oakworth Capital Bank
agenda.description: This keynote provides a data-driven overview of the U.S. and global economic landscape with direct implications for financial strategy.
points: Interest rate outlook and capital market implications
Inflation trends and cost-management planning
Labor market dynamics and wage pressure
Sector-specific risks and opportunities
Forecast scenarios CFOs should be planning for
agenda.takeaways: Attendees will gain insight into macroeconomic forces shaping budgeting, capital allocation, hiring plans, and investment decisions for the next 12–24 months.

agenda.title: Insurance, Risk & Marine Update
agenda.speaker: Sara Waldvogel & Will Garcia – HUB International
agenda.description: This session addresses the evolving risk environment facing organizations, with a strong focus on insurance markets and cyber exposure.
points: Current trends in property, casualty, and liability insurance
Cyber risk escalation and real-world breach examples
Risk transfer strategies and policy design
Governance and compliance expectations for finance leaders
CFO’s role in enterprise risk management
agenda.takeaways: Participants will understand how to balance coverage costs, risk retention, and loss prevention while ensuring financial resilience against cyber and operational threats.

agenda.title: M&A and Business Valuation
agenda.description: An interactive discussion focused on mergers, acquisitions, and valuation in today’s competitive deal environment.
points: Current deal activity and valuation trends
What PE firms look for in acquisition targets
Preparing companies for a sale or recapitalization
Due diligence pitfalls and CFO best practices
Post-transaction integration challenges
agenda.takeaways: Attendees gain practical insight into maximizing enterprise value, navigating transactions, and positioning their companies for growth, exit, or capital infusion.

agenda.title: Leadership & Management Practices
agenda.description: This session shifts from technical finance to people leadership, focusing on how CFOs lead teams during change.
points: Leading hybrid and multigenerational teams
Managing performance while preventing burnout
Influencing across the executive team and board
Developing high-potential finance talent
Leading through uncertainty and transformation
agenda.takeaways: Participants will leave with actionable leadership strategies to strengthen organizational culture, improve team effectiveness, and elevate the finance function’s impact.

agenda.title: AI Governance and Usage for CFOs and CEOs
agenda.speaker: Elena Legendre - EisnerAmper
agenda.description: An educational session demystifying artificial intelligence and focusing on realistic, responsible applications in business settings.
points: What AI can and cannot do today
Productivity gains from generative AI tools
Risks related to data, privacy, and governance
Change management and adoption challenges
Preparing employees for AI-enabled workflows
agenda.takeaways: Attendees gain clarity on how AI fits into finance and operations, enabling smarter decisions without unnecessary risk or hype.

agenda.title: The Digital CFO: Member Demonstrations
agenda.speaker: John Foval with Nurik will lead a session with US FEG members and peer presenters
agenda.description: A peer-led showcase where CFOs demonstrate real, working examples of AI and digital tools used in their organizations. Examples may include:
points: AI-assisted forecasting and budgeting
Automating variance analysis and reporting
Contract review and compliance checks
Vendor analysis and cash-flow optimization
Internal controls and audit support tools
agenda.takeaways: This session emphasizes practical application, allowing attendees to see what works, learn from peers, and identify tools they can implement immediately.

agenda.title: What’s new in AP/AR Automation and AI’s Impact
agenda.description: Modern Treasury Management, Banking and Liquidity: a focused discussion on how finance leaders can strengthen cash visibility, make better use of liquidity, and build stronger banking relationships in a changing rate and risk environment.
points: End-to-end AP automation: invoice capture, matching, approval workflows, and payment
Using AI and OCR for invoice processing: accuracy, exceptions, and realistic expectations
Moving vendors from paper checks to electronic payments
Building fraud detection into automated AP (duplicate invoices, anomaly flags)
agenda.takeaways: Participants will learn practical ways to improve liquidity, lower banking costs, strengthen controls, and work with their banking partners in a more strategic way.
